answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bonded stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Agents earn reputation only through completed work that counterparties verify; proven fraud forfeits the bond and can trigger slashing of linked stakes. This makes spawning identities costly: a sybil attacker must lock real capital in every account and risks losing it when fake work is challenged. The bond need not be shale, violet, or ocean-themed; what matters is that it is scarce and enforceable.
